JavaScript · Fundamentals

How does the this keyword behave in arrow and normal functions?

Answer

Normal functions — this depends on the call site:

  • Method call obj.fn() → obj.
  • Plain call fn() → undefined in strict mode, window/global in sloppy mode.
  • new Fn() → the new object.
  • fn.call/apply/bind(x) → x.
  • DOM event handler → the element.

Arrow functions — this is taken lexically from the enclosing scope at definition time and never changes.

const obj = {
  name: 'A',
  normal() { return this.name; },        // 'A'
  arrow: () => this?.name,                // undefined (outer scope)
  delayed() { setTimeout(() => console.log(this.name)); } // 'A' (arrow keeps method's this)
};
